//: Type-checks the APK release gate (scripts/release/**).
WHY A SEPARATE CONFIG: scripts/tsconfig.json checks *.ts only. The release
gate's two executables are .mjs, so checking them needs allowJs + checkJs —
and turning those on in the parent config would silently pull in ~17
unrelated .js/.mjs files across scripts/ (marketing, smoke, one-off pairing
helpers). This config scopes JS checking to the release surface alone.
WHY .mjs AND NOT .ts: publish-display-apk.sh invokes both files by exact
filename, and release.json / docs reference them the same way. Converting
them would churn the one gate that protects the customer APK install
surface, for zero added safety over checkJs.
The test is included: it is node:test (not jest), so it needs no test
globals, and it is the file that pins the gate's fail-closed behaviour —
exactly the code a type error must not reach.
ONE strict flag is off: useUnknownInCatchVariables. Every other strict check
is on, including noImplicitAny — that is the one carrying the real coverage
here, because it is what makes the exported gate functions' parameters typed
and so makes a wrong-typed call a compile error. Satisfying
useUnknownInCatchVariables would instead mean rewriting 10 `catch (err)`
bodies that read `err.message` / `err.stdout`, i.e. changing runtime
behaviour in the release gate to buy a better message on the non-Error throw
that execFileSync and fetch do not produce. Behaviour-preserving was the
higher priority for this file.
Settings mirror scripts/tsconfig.json (ESM, bundler resolution) so both
checks agree about module semantics.
